settings.title: Types of AC Problems We Repair

settings.editor:
If your air conditioner is running but the air feels warm, the problem may be related to low refrigerant, a dirty coil, airflow restrictions, thermostat issues, or compressor trouble.

Our technicians inspect the full cooling system to determine whether the issue is simple, such as a clogged filter, or more serious, such as a refrigerant leak or failing component. Repairing the cause early can help restore cooling and reduce strain on your system.

Weak airflow can make certain rooms uncomfortable even when your AC is running. This may be caused by a dirty air filter, blower motor problems, blocked vents, ductwork issues, frozen coils, or airflow restrictions inside the system.

Professional AC repair can help improve air movement, reduce hot spots, and help your cooling system keep your home more comfortable during Central Iowa summers.

If your AC will not start, the issue may involve the thermostat, electrical connections, capacitor, contactor, circuit breaker, or outdoor condenser unit.

Our technicians check the electrical and mechanical components carefully so you are not left guessing. Once we identify the source, we explain the repair clearly and help you understand your options.

Short cycling happens when your AC turns on and off too often without completing a full cooling cycle. This can increase energy use, reduce comfort, and place extra wear on the system.

Common causes include thermostat issues, restricted airflow, low refrigerant, overheating components, or an improperly sized system. Addressing short cycling quickly can help prevent larger cooling system repairs.

settings.title: Frozen AC Coils or Refrigerant Lines

settings.editor:
Ice on your AC system is not normal during cooling season. Frozen coils may point to restricted airflow, low refrigerant levels, dirty coils, or blower motor issues.

If your system freezes, it should be inspected before being run heavily again. Continuing to operate a frozen AC can increase the risk of compressor damage and more expensive repairs.

Air conditioners remove moisture from the air as they cool your home. That moisture should drain safely away from the system. If you see water around your indoor unit, the issue may be a clogged condensate drain, frozen coil, damaged drain pan, or installation issue.

AC water leaks should be addressed quickly to prevent water damage and restore proper moisture removal.

Your AC should not bang, clank, buzz loudly, or give off burning or musty odors. These symptoms can point to loose components, electrical issues, motor problems, mold or moisture buildup, or failing parts.

Our technicians can inspect the system, identify the source, and recommend the safest repair before the issue gets worse.
Tell us what you're hearing or feeling and we'll work it out.
